searchText: Hey! Unfortunately, there's no such functionality in Gitter. The available actions are: - removing the room - changing a room tagline (current is "Java implementation of the Ethereum protocol") - exporting room data (users, messages) i think it's fine to remove the room given the client is no longer being developed after checking with the repo owners i would also archive the room history for posterity <@&595685821026271242> not sure if there is anything to be done about this, but it seems like this server is seeing more and more users who are pretty removed from the purpose of the server but they want to share their 2 cents. This seems to happen most commonly in <#745077610685661265>. I feel like I'm skipping almost every third message in a discussion there because the posts are barely relevant to the discussion at hand. yup, threw up a message a few minutes ago related to that. One option that we’re looking to explore on the Ethereum.org discord is just reordering the channels. Lazy users will post in the first channel that they think *might* be suitable for their query so having a buffer ‘general’ channel before allcoredevs might help with this. Other than that - required roles to post in certain channels (which, whilst it would work, I don’t love the idea of) This actually isn’t a bad idea! Anyone can still read, but write access people almost all have a role already (EG. Client teams) Well if there was a mechanism for getting added to the role that had 100% acceptance I think that would probably create *just enough* friction to remove the majority of low value posts without closing the possibility of open discourse On second thought, closing it off to accepted participants is probably better... Team <@&861652182781001758> now has a discord flair 😄 I’m so happy I found this invite! Dinally@ Quick question 🙋🏻‍♂️- if miners on the current PoW chain decided to spend their ETH hiring devs, working on exchange compliance, and keeping ETH 1.0 alive could this actually happen? Is there a fear the original or “authentic” ETH could pose a threat to ETH 2.0??

excerpts.author: aldekein
excerpts.content:
Hey! Unfortunately, there's no such functionality in Gitter. The available actions are:
- removing the room
- changing a room tagline (current is "Java implementation of the Ethereum protocol")
- exporting room data (users, messages)

excerpts.author: joshuaisbuilding
excerpts.content: One option that we’re looking to explore on the Ethereum.org discord is just reordering the channels. Lazy users will post in the first channel that they think *might* be suitable for their query so having a buffer ‘general’ channel before allcoredevs might help with this.

excerpts.author: joshuaisbuilding
excerpts.content: Other than that - required roles to post in certain channels (which, whilst it would work, I don’t love the idea of)

excerpts.author: trent_vanepps
excerpts.content: This actually isn’t a bad idea! Anyone can still read, but write access people almost all have a role already (EG. Client teams)

excerpts.author: joshuaisbuilding
excerpts.content: Well if there was a mechanism for getting added to the role that had 100% acceptance I think that would probably create *just enough* friction to remove the majority of low value posts without closing the possibility of open discourse

excerpts.author: joshuaisbuilding
excerpts.content: On second thought, closing it off to accepted participants is probably better...
